claims: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026.
Artemis II was a 10-day mission around the Moon.
The Artemis II Orion capsule was recovered by the U.S. Navy vessel USS John P. Murtha.
Artemis II was the first crewed lunar flyby in 50 years.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down on April 10, 2026, at 5:07 p.m. PDT.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down on April 11, 00:07:27 UTC.
The recovery site of the Artemis II Orion spacecraft was the Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft traveled roughly 250,000 miles from Earth.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft traveled about 5,000 miles beyond the Moon before returning.
NASA's AROW system tracked the Artemis II Orion spacecraft.
The Artemis II Orion capsule will be transported back to Kennedy Space Center in Florida for inspection.
The Artemis II mission concluded on April 10, 2026.
